The user wants to buy two tickets: a musical ticket for "Mamma Mia" on next Friday, and a train ticket from New York to Chicago on the same day. We need to call the appropriate function twice.

We have two relevant functions: musical_ticket_buy(show, date) and train_ticket_buy(origin, destination, date). The user didn't specify the date explicitly but said "next Friday". We need to interpret that as the upcoming Friday relative to today (which is 2026-11-04). Today is Thursday, so next Friday is 2026-11-05. So we will use date "2026-11-05".

We also need to confirm the origin and destination: "紐約" is New York, "芝加哥" is Chicago. So origin: "New York", destination: "Chicago".

We need to call both functions. According to policy, we can only call one function at a time. But we can chain calls? The policy says we cannot call multiple functions in a single response. We need to do them sequentially. We can first call musical_ticket_buy with show="Mamma Mia", date="2026-11-05". Then after receiving the result, we can call train_ticket_buy with origin="New York", destination="Chicago", date="2026-11-05". Or vice versa. The order doesn't matter. We'll do musical first then train.

We need to output the function calls in JSON format. The assistant's response should contain the function call. After calling, we get a response from the tool. Then we respond with the result. The policy says we should not mention the function name or arguments again. Just give the result.

So step 1: call musical_ticket_buy({"show":"Mamma Mia","date":"2026-11-05"}).

Then we get a response. Then we call train_ticket_buy({"origin":"New York","destination":"Chicago","date":"2026-11-05"}).

After each call, we provide the result. The user might want confirmation. We should provide the results. Also we should ask if they want anything else.
